title: How a Sink P-Trap Prevents Sewer Gas Entry
description: The P-trap under a sink is a fundamental component of sanitary plumbing designed to maintain a fluid barrier between the living space and the drainage network. After water flows down the fixture drain, a small portion remains trapped in the lower dip of the trap bend. This trapped water forms a continuous liquid seal that blocks foul-smelling and potentially dangerous sewer gases from traveling up through the drain opening. For the trap to function correctly, it must be properly vented. Proper venting equalizes air pressure within the drainage system, preventing siphonage from pulling the protective water seal out during heavy discharge downstream.

How a Sink P-Trap Prevents Sewer Gas Entry

The P-trap under a sink is a fundamental component of sanitary plumbing designed to maintain a fluid barrier between the living space and the drainage network. After water flows down the fixture drain, a small portion remains trapped in the lower dip of the trap bend. This trapped water forms a continuous liquid seal that blocks foul-smelling and potentially dangerous sewer gases from traveling up through the drain opening. For the trap to function correctly, it must be properly vented. Proper venting equalizes air pressure within the drainage system, preventing siphonage from pulling the protective water seal out during heavy discharge downstream.
